anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, both circular CAN connectors use the same global labels for their differential pair: J17 (CAN Interface A) pins 2/3 are NET0142/NET0010, and J18 (CAN Interface B) pins 2/3 are also NET0142/NET0010.
anomalies.expected: The specification calls for two isolated CAN buses (CAN0 and CAN1), each with its own transceiver and broken out to a separate connector. The two connectors should therefore carry independent CAN_H/CAN_L nets, not the same pair.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: J17 'CAN Interface A' pins 2 NET0142, 3 NET0010; J18 'CAN Interface B' pins 2 NET0142, 3 NET0010.
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ... and J13

anomalies.impact: The two CAN buses are shorted together on the connector side. They cannot operate independently; one transceiver/controller effectively drives both buses, and bus termination/contention will prevent correct CAN0/CAN1 communication.

anomalies.observed: Both MCP2515 CAN controllers are drawn with identical SPI/status global labels: U45 has SCK NET0052, S1 NET0180, S0 NET0152, CS NET0049; U39 has the same labels on the corresponding pins.
anomalies.expected: Each MCP2515 should have its own chip-select net (and ideally separate SPI/status nets) so the host can address CAN0 and CAN1 controllers independently.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U45 pins labeled S1 NET0180, S0 NET0152, CS NET0049, SCK NET0052; later CAN BUS sheet: U39 pins labeled S1 NET0180, S0 NET0152, CS NET0049, SCK NET0052.
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: The two SPI CAN controllers are tied together on the same SPI bus with a common CS. Both devices will be selected simultaneously and their SPI/status outputs will contend, making independent control of the two CAN buses impossible.

anomalies.observed: No CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays are visible on the CAN differential pairs. The references D9 and D10 in the drawing are used elsewhere as an LED_RED and a 28 V zener, not as CAN TVS arrays.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that D9 and D10 are CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N and CAN1_P/N for CAN bus transient/ESD protection.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N | CAN bus transient/ESD protection
LEDs sheet: D9 is LED_RED; PoE sheet: D10 is 28V/500mW zener; no CDSOT23-SM712 parts are shown on the CAN BUS sheets.

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses lack the specified transient/ESD protection, reducing robustness against ESD and voltage transients on the external CAN cabling.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows clear deviations from the intended two independent CAN buses: both CAN connectors share the same CAN differential-pair labels, and both MCP2515 controllers share the same SPI/CS labels. The specified CAN TVS arrays also appear to be absent.
